newsitem.title: UK: Dollar/yen steady below week's high before G7 meet.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/yen steady below week's high before G7 meet.

text.p: The dollar hovered below this week's high against the yen before the beginning of the three-day summit of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations.
Speculation the summit would become a forum for the U.S. to criticise Japan for a rebound in its trade surpluses waned in the wake of comments made Thursday by U.S. President Bill Clinton.

Clinton said he was concerned about Japan's large trade surplus with the U.S., but added that Japan was taking steps to boost domestic demand and that exchange rates should not be used as a means of correcting trade balances.
Still, traders said they would remain wary of pushing the dollar aggressively higher until after the G7.
"The market looks very nervous ahead of the G7," said Craig Justham, the deputy manager of foreign exchange at Creditanstalt Bankverein.
The dollar was quoted at 1.7250/55 at 0800 GMT from 1.7246/56 late Thursday in Europe. It was at 114.48/58 compared with 114.13/23 yesterday and the 114.85 high it reached Monday.
U.S. calls for Japan to stimulate domestic demand to keep its trade surplus in check come as a report Friday showed a decline in Japan's index of leading economic indicators.
The diffusion index of leading economic indicators fell to 5.6 in April from 36.4 in March while the index of coincident indicators was down at 10 from 81.8 in March.

An official at Japan's Economic Planning Agency said the country's diffusion index of coincident economic indicators is likely to be above 50 in May. Still, the index of leading economic indicators will likely remain below this boom-or-bust mark.
The Bank of Japan's monthly report said Friday the economy is continuing to recover gradually, even though consumption has fallen in reaction to an increase in consumption tax in April.

The mark was bolstered against the dollar after a report showed German M3 money supply grew at an annual rate of 7.0 percent in May from the fourth quarter of 1996. That was outside the central bank's 3.5 to 6.5 percent target range and above economists' expectations of a 6.2 percent annual growth rate.
Still, the dollar quickly stabilised and traders don't expect it to fall below the 1.72-mark support level which held overnight.
The dollar was undermined against the mark Thursday and in overnight trading Friday as the mark gained as much as 1.9 percent against the yen.

"Mark/yen moves have brought dollar/mark down here and there was a bit of selling (of dollars) on the back of the M3," said Keith Lewis, the manager of treasury markets at Amex Bank. "But from here on I would favour the upside."
Mark/yen was at 66.42/45 from 66.19/22 late Thursday. -Swaha Pattanaik, London newsroom +44 171 542 6284
